quantity.note: The 4850 Level is named for its depth in feet: 4850 ft x 0.3048 m/ft = 1478.3 m, the figure SURF itself gives ('4850 Level (1478 m)') and the one the local map uses. SURF's scientific director rounds it to 1500 m in the Snowmass 2022 paper ("campuses at the 4850-foot level (1500 m, 4300 m.w.e.)"); the same author gives 1490 m in a 2024 paper, and DUNE TDR Vol. I says "approximately 1.5 km underground". The water-equivalent overburden is the separate 4300 m.w.e. value. The far-detector modules are on the 4850 Level of SURF. CHANGED 2026-10-25: was value 1500 m, display "1500 m of rock (4850-foot level)" (the Snowmass 2022 rounding), which disagreed with the 1478 m of the map level. Placement of the DUNE far detector at this level: DUNE TDR Vol. I, §1.1.2 and Fig. 1.4 (arXiv PDF p. 25): "the SURF underground area, also referred to as the 4850 (foot) level or 4850L"; ProtoDUNE-SP paper (arXiv:2007.06722, PDF p. 12): "a far detector located at the 4850 ft level of Sanford Underground Research Facility (SURF)". The quote above is SURF's statement for the 4850 Level itself.

summary.plain: A very large experiment that will send neutrinos 1285 kilometres through the Earth from Illinois to South Dakota, where detectors filled with liquid argon a mile underground will record them. It aims to find out whether neutrinos and antineutrinos behave differently, to catch neutrinos from an exploding star, and to look for protons decaying.
summary.technical: Long-baseline accelerator-neutrino experiment hosted by Fermilab: a 1.0-1.2 MW wide-band on-axis beam from 60-120 GeV Main Injector protons, a composite near detector at Fermilab and four 10 kt fiducial LArTPC far-detector modules at the 4850 Level of SURF, 1285 km away. Physics drivers are leptonic CP violation, the mass ordering, supernova-burst neutrinos and nucleon decay.
